body:
Cluely is an AI assistant that runs in a hidden window on a user's computer and feeds suggested answers in real time during interviews, sales calls, meetings and exams. It was built by Roy Lee and Neel Shanmugam, who started out at Columbia University, and launched on 20 April 2025.

Where it came from

The earlier project was Interview Coder, a Chrome extension that gave AI-generated solutions to LeetCode-style problems during technical interviews. Columbia suspended Lee over it, and he later left the university. Cluely widened the idea from coding interviews to any live conversation.

What the product does

The assistant listens to the conversation, reads what is on screen and shows suggestions in an overlay that is designed not to appear when you share your screen. The company's pitch is that AI should be an everyday aid rather than something you hide, while critics describe it as a tool for cheating.

Money and growth

  • Seed funding of US$5.3 million from Abstract Ventures and Susa Ventures.
  • US$15 million from Andreessen Horowitz, bringing total funding to about US$20.3 million at a valuation reported near US$120 million.
  • 70,000 sign-ups in the first week after launch, according to press coverage, and later reports of about US$6 million in annual recurring revenue.

Is Cluely legitimate?

As a business, yes: it is a registered, venture-backed company with named founders, a public launch date and investors including Andreessen Horowitz. The open question is not whether the company is real but whether using the product is allowed where you plan to use it. Employers, schools and exam bodies often ban undisclosed AI help, so check the rules first.

The argument

The question is not whether the software works but where it may be used. Many employers and universities treat undisclosed AI help in an assessment as misconduct. Anyone considering it should read the rules of the interview, course or platform first.

What we have not verified

These figures come from press reports and interviews; confirm current numbers with the company.
